editorial.headline: On-Street Parking: Nationally Open, Including in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 52214 covers the operation of parking on the roadway itself, open to every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
On-street parking is a specific urban service: the organisation of parking conducted on the roadway itself. KBLI 52214 is therefore about managing the use of street space for vehicles, rather than treating parking as an abstract add-on to another activity. Its focus is clear and bounded—parking that takes place on the road body.

The activity is available at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That breadth matters because it lets the same defined activity be registered across the full range of business sizes recognised in the record. The national position is equally direct: it is TERBUKA for PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record places no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity.

Bali does not reverse that national openness. A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today; it is not blocked by the province-wide PMA moratorium. The moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA across the island, permanently, but this activity is recorded as outside that block. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—Medium-High/High—which is why the moratorium does not prevent its registration.

That distinction is the essential reading of the code. National openness is real, and Bali remains available rather than merely theoretically possible. The Bali position does not introduce a separate foreign-ownership percentage or partnership condition in this record. Instead, it turns on the stated risk treatment at the Besar scale: the activity sits beyond the category captured by the island-wide moratorium. For a founder considering an on-street parking operation, the regulatory picture presented here is therefore unusually plain: full foreign ownership is permitted nationally, and Bali does not block PMA registration for this activity.
